Package com.acxiom.emailaudit.rules

Class RuleResult

java.lang.Object
com.acxiom.emailaudit.rules.RuleResult
public final class RuleResult extends Object
Immutable value object returned by every AuditRule execution.

Structure

  RuleResult
   ├─ ruleId          – which rule produced this result
   ├─ status          – PASS | FAIL | ERROR | SKIPPED
   ├─ severity        – inherited from the rule at creation time
   ├─ findings        – zero or more human-readable finding messages
   ├─ businessImpact  – status-aware impact statement, from
   │                    AuditRule#passImpact() or AuditRule#failImpact()
   ├─ errorMessage    – populated only when status == ERROR
   ├─ durationMs      – wall-clock execution time in milliseconds
   └─ evaluatedAt     – UTC instant the result was created

Building results

Use the static factory methods rather than the builder directly where the intent is obvious:


 // Simple pass
 return RuleResult.pass(rule);

 // One or more findings
 return RuleResult.fail(rule, startMs, List.of("Missing alt on 3 images"));

 // Internal rule error
 return RuleResult.error(rule, startMs, e);

 // Skipped (rule disabled or precondition not met)
 return RuleResult.skipped(rule, "No images found on page");

Business impact

Every RuleResult carries a status-aware business impact statement, resolved automatically at construction time from the originating AuditRule: AuditRule.passImpact() when status == PASS, otherwise AuditRule.failImpact() (this covers FAIL, ERROR, and SKIPPED). No call site needs to set this explicitly — it is derived the same way ruleId/severity already are, inside RuleResult.Builder's constructor.
